subject: Commercial proposal: phased onramp, rollback triggers, and credit matrix
messages:
From: Alex Roberts <alex@altcore.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re-evaluating inference vendors — pricing & operational questions

Neha,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As mentioned, AltCore is evaluating a replacement for our current inference stack. Two things we need to validate quickly: a) whether Redwood will match a blended economic that the incumbent is offering across runtime and egress, and b) whether there are any operational surcharges for KV cache invalidations and multi-tenant burst behavior.

Attached is a short snapshot of last 6 months' usage (token distribution + peak windows). Our procurement team would like a clear price/credit comparison and a concise runbook for a fast migration (pilot -> scale) that doesn't expose us to unexpected overages during cutover.

High-level asks:
- Can you propose a price match or a structured concession?
- What does the rollback / escape trigger look like if we see regressions post-cutover?
- Any limits on concurrent bursting and a heads-up on how KV cache cold-starts are handled (and billed)?

Timeline: pilot starting mid-May; commercial decision by end of June.

Appreciate a short proposal/term outline we can share internally.

Best,
Alex

Attachment: altcore_comp_comparison.pdf (1.2MB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Roberts <alex@altcore.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating inference vendors — pricing & operational questions

Alex — thanks for the summary and the usage snapshot. I pulled together two commercial options for AltCore that balance price, runway risk, and operational safety. High-level first, then a quick note on the KV cache / burst behavior.

Option A — Short pilot, step-up commit
- 3-month pilot (no minimum) + 9-month committed term if successful
- Pilot pricing: usage at list -10% to keep migration friction low
- If convert to 12-month commit within pilot: 18% off list + $40k onboarding/egress bridge credits
- Rollback / escape trigger: if production token-level P99 latency increases >25% or availability <99.0% for two consecutive weekly windows, AltCore can exercise a rollback clause to pause committed billing for up to 30 days while we remediate.

Option B — Deeper commit, better unit economics
- 24-month commitment with upfront billing cadence (quarterly)
- 30% off list + $120k migration credit (applied as bill credits over first 6 months)
- SLA window: availability target 99.5%; if missed, additional credits escalate per the SLA schedule.

Operational notes (KV cache / burst behavior)
- KV cache: We perform per-customer prefix caching; cold-starts are not billed as a separate line item but will show in peak token consumption. For high burst scenarios we can configure dedicated pre-warmed pools as part of Redwood Dedicated (surcharge applies if you require reserved pre-warm for pilot cutover).
- We call out the surcharge as an optional line: dedicated pre-warm pool = one-time setup $15k + prorated hourly for reserved GPUs during the warm window.
- For multi-tenant hosted customers, we auto-throttle to protect tenant SLOs; when you need guaranteed burst capacity we recommend the reserved pool above.

Next steps
1) If either option looks promising, we can produce a binding commercial term sheet and a short migration runbook (cutover checklist + KV cache warm-up steps).
2) I pasted the relevant usage assumptions into the attachment altcore_usage_snapshot.csv and flagged expected peak windows.

Would you prefer Option A to keep the pilot simple, or should I put together a 24-month economics sheet for the CFO?

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Neha — this is helpful, thanks. A few clarifying points from procurement and infra: 

- The incumbent has offered a phased discount ladder: 10% pilot, 25% post-commit, with a 60-day rollback window and no separate pre-warm fees. To be competitive, we need a counter that preserves a short pilot and limits upfront cash.
- Can you tighten the rollback trigger to be actioned by a mutual ops runbook (we'll sign off on the runbook) and limit the rollback window to 14 days instead of 30?
- Regarding the pre-warm pool: we don't want a $15k one-time fee if possible; would Redwood be willing to convert some of the migration credit to cover the pre-warm setup cost?
- Also: how do you handle prorated billing if we seat-split during the onboarding month (some seats opt in mid-month)?

If you can update Option A to reflect a 14-day rollback and a migration-credit cover for pre-warm, plus pricing row on prorated seat billing, this will help move the conversation with our CFO.

Best,
Alex
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re-evaluating inference vendors — pricing & operational questions

Marissa, Neha — forwarding AltCore's reply. Quick internal play: I can approve converting up to $15k of the $40k onboarding credit in Option A to cover the pre-warm setup for the pilot (keeps cash outlay minimal for them). We should keep the rollback window tight (14 days) but add a clause that rollback must be preceded by a mutual runbook sign-off and two joint incident debug sessions. That reduces our exposure while giving them the operational guarantee they want.

Suggested language for term sheet (short):
- Pilot: no minimum, 3 months.
- Conversion: if customer signs commit within pilot, apply 18% list discount and $25k onboarding credit (remaining $15k reserved to cover pre-warm pool).
- Rollback: customer may invoke rollback within 14 days after conversion if runbook-certified regressions (P99 latency + availability thresholds) persist after two joint debug sessions; rollback pauses committed billing and preserves data transfer credits for 30 days.

Marissa — please confirm we can publish this as a one-time concession for AltCore in HubSpot (deal ALT-4382). If approved I'll send the updated commercial term sheet and a short onboarding runbook draft to Alex.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
